digest.component_or_area: LLM provider seam and model routing infrastructure
propositions: rebar's LLM runtime branches on provider name strings (anthropic detection) rather than using a pluggable provider factory, creating tightly coupled, non-extensible code paths for caching, retrying, output modes and structured output.

Bedrock-hosted Claude has no first-class support path; the only workaround (PR #121) wraps Bedrock in an OpenAI-compatible gateway proxy, losing prompt caching, native retry transport, per-request timeouts and structured output capabilities.

Documentation claims REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY work for custom endpoints, but code at runner.py:653 actively rejects them; the documentation is false and the config fields are parsed but unused.

The signed verdict sidecar records a model string that no longer names the actual provider when routed through a gateway; consumers cannot distinguish first-class verdicts from best-effort ones or detect capability gaps.

Anthropic and Bedrock have different capability profiles (prompt caching support, tool caching, structured output modes) but the code selects output mode and cache behavior by matching provider name strings, ignoring the actual provider's declared capabilities.

Retry behavior, timeout configuration and prompt caching are provider-specific (botocore config for Bedrock vs httpx AsyncTenacityTransport for Anthropic) but selected by hardcoded branches; equivalent guarantees across providers require per-transport parity measurement.
